newsitem.title: QATAR: U.S. warplanes land in Qatar.
newsitem.headline: U.S. warplanes land in Qatar.

text.p: Thirty U.S. warplanes landed in Qatar on Thursday on a temporary deployment to show Washington's commitment to protecting moderate Gulf states, officials and diplomats said.
The Airpower Expeditionary Force, to stay in Doha until May 20, includes F-15Es from Seymour Johnson Air Force Base in North Carolina and F-16s from three bases in South Carolina and New Mexico.
They join some 200 U.S. jets permanently stationed in the Gulf region as protection against Iran and Iraq and will fly missions in support of "Operation Southern Watch" over Iraq.
This enforces a no-fly zone over southern Iraq declared by Western powers in 1992.
The planes, designed for ground attack and aerial combat with other jets, will also help train Qatari airforce pilots.

"The deployment comes as part of the U.S.-Qatar defence cooperation agreement to strengthen the long-term working relationship between the two forces," a Qatari foreign ministry official said. "It is not aimed against any other parties and is non-aggressive in nature."
A U.S. official added: "The mission is to hone the ability of the forces to respond to crises swiftly and sharply."
